transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card services. My name is Marcus. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?
Customer: Hello, my name is Joanna Prentiss.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Ms. Prentiss. Before we get started, could you verify the billing address on file and the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Sure, it's 318 Larchmont Lane, and the card ends in 4109.
Agent: Thank you for verifying that. What can I help you with today?
Customer: Well, I noticed a charge for $230.00 that I definitely didn't make myself.
Agent: I can look into that for you. What date does that show for, and what is the merchant name listed?
Customer: It shows up on September 27th, and the name on it is PixelForge Games.
Agent: Got it, September 27th for $230.00 at PixelForge Games. Do you recognize that company or know what it might be for?
Customer: I didn't at first, but I did some asking around the house. It turns out my teenage son took my credit card right out of my purse and bought a bunch of in-game items.
Agent: I see. Has he ever had permission to use this card in the past?
Customer: No, never. I have never let him touch my card or use it for anything.
Agent: Does he normally have access to your card or your wallet?
Customer: My purse was just sitting on the kitchen counter. He must have slipped it out while I was outside, typed the numbers into his game, and then put it back.
Agent: Did you speak with him about this, or have you tried reaching out to PixelForge Games directly?
Customer: I talked to him and he confessed right away. I haven't contacted the game company, though, I just came straight to you.
Agent: Understood. So to make sure I have all the facts straight, on September 27th there was a $230.00 charge from PixelForge Games, which your son made after taking the card from your purse without your knowledge or consent, and you have never allowed him to use your card.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
